column1: # exemptions.tsv — every exemption a check makes, with a reason and an end date.
# A rule without exceptions is a rule people route around; an exception nobody
# wrote down is a rule that quietly stopped applying. Three checks carried
# hard-coded exemption lists before this file existed, none of them with a
# reason, and two had silently gone stale: one named a file that had moved, and
# one was missing a sibling test written after the list. Both failures looked
# like the guard working.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   check    which check reads the row (its own name, no path)
#   pattern  what to exempt; each check interprets this in its own terms
#            (check-em-dash: a regex of text that is not prose;
#             check-space-boundary: a path prefix of a file allowed to carry
#             the literals the guard hunts for)
#   expires  YYYY-MM-DD, or "structural"
#   reason   why. Required. Write it for the person who finds this in a year.
# "structural" is not a waiver. It marks a case where the rule was stated too
# broadly and this row is part of its real definition, so there is nothing to
# come back to. Anything that is a temporary allowance gets a date, and
# check-exemptions reports it as OVERDUE once that date passes.
# check
em-dash
column4: A long CLI flag is not prose. The ban is on punctuation a reader sees as a dash; --no-verify and --dry-run are code that happens to live in a sentence. The header of check-em-dash promised this exemption from the start and the code never had it, so commit messages naming a flag were refused for punctuation they did not contain.

column1: space-boundary
column4: The guard necessarily contains the literals it searches for, in its own patterns and comments. It cannot be made to not match itself.

column1: space-boundary
column4: Exercises the guard, so it contains the same literals on purpose.

column1: space-boundary
column4: Scaffolds a real space in the real vault for the length of its run (see its header), so during that window the fixture owner is a genuine paspoort entry and the guard finds the literal again in the test that created it.

column1: space-boundary
column4: Carries owner literals in its own detection patterns, for the same reason as the guard itself.
